Name: Hauling: A Message Ten Years Late
MissionBoardDescription: Private Contract. Take a message from the <Alias=TargetLocation> on <Alias=TargetPlanetLocation> to someone in the same system. Payment on completion.

LogEntries.Entry: An old salvager at the <Alias=TargetLocation> wants a message carried to his former partner in the same system. They haven't spoken in years.
The salvager gave me a message for his old partner: the ship is hers, and he was wrong about the engine. I need to take it to her.
I gave his old partner the message. She's going to fetch the ship herself.
I told his old partner he was wrong about the engine before anything else. She's going to go and see him.

Objectives.DisplayText: Talk to the old salvager at the <Alias=TargetLocation>
Give the message to his old partner at the <Alias=FinalLocation>

Lines.ResponseText: We stripped wrecks together half our lives, then stopped speaking over an engine. There's something she should hear, and I'm the wrong one to say it.
Two things. The ship's hers; my eyes have gone and I can't fly it. And I was wrong about the engine. She'll know what that means.
What was wrong with the engine?
She said it was running hot and I said she was fussing. We lost the ship we had before this one. Nobody was hurt. That was luck, not me.
Because the last time I tried, I said the wrong thing first. Say it how you like. You'll do it better than me.
You'll be the one carrying it. It isn't a long message.
If you're selling something, I'm not buying.
Not selling? Then you're carrying something, and there's only one man who'd send me a courier instead of calling. Go on, then. What did he say?
The ship's yours, and he was wrong about the engine.
Wrong about the engine. Ten years, and he puts it second. I'll come and get the ship myself. He can have the coffee on.
He was wrong about the engine. And the ship's yours.
He said wrong, out loud? That's all I wanted. The ship can wait a day. I'm going to go and see him.
He sounded like he meant it.
He always does. That was never the problem.
Not once. I hear him on the general channel now and then, complaining about the weather.
